searchText: Hello guys. I have questions the terms differences between signed execution payload by validators & beacon block. These are same data? or have some differences? Beacon block contains a field "execution payload", is that what you meant? Yeah may be. Then beacon block is another term of `slot`?? No, a slot is a period of 12 seconds. It can contain a beacon block, but it can also be empty (e g. proposer failed to propose a block in time) slot != beacon block. beacon block contains execution payload. execution payload != beacon block. Got it. <@567563309327581194> Just wanted to say I tried some L2’s and the fees were indeed killer. Polygon is cents but rollups (arbitrum) cost me dollars which was very surprising given that I expected it to be cheap. Went back to using polygon. I heard that there going to use other methods to make rollups use less gas in the future but I can only comment on my experience from last month. optimism is intentionally throttled at the moment not sure about arbitrum Does the throttling have a big impact on tx costs? I thought optimistic rollups were rather linear in how they scale, as opposed to the log-scaling zk-rollups I'm not sure of the specifics but I believe there is a linear component to the fee structure in both cases due to the L1 data availability I can look into the specifics in a bit if you want On Optimism, there is a 200k transactions / day limit after which they start throttling with higher gas prices. It was 100k / day previously. However, all of this doesn't matter because Optimism never processed more than 53k transactions a day as can be seen here: https://optimistic.etherscan.io/chart/tx As to transaction costs, it's quite complicated as they use some form of their own gas, but as a general idea the cost of a L2 transaction is ~98% mainnet dependent. The Sequencer itself charges cents just like the sidechains. not sure if they throttle, but Arbitrum Nitro seems to be client changes that'll lead to higher capacity. is there something about calldata compression that makes it quite hard, or is it more likely it's just a lower priority for the teams? has any ORU implemented any calldata compression yet? > is there something about calldata compression that makes it quite hard there's a few tricks you can do, but they're still special cases things like ether/erc20/erc721 transfers can be reduced a lot by doing lookups into the state with a proof when doing the fraud game, which adds complexity to the fraud proof verifier, but in the general case there isn't much you can do and have to put all the calldata there and execute it normally with zk rollups all of that proving happens off chain but it still has that extra complexity zksync *started* with only token transfers and doing those optimizations so it's already pretty small

excerpts.author: johnydony
excerpts.content:
Hello guys. 
I have questions the terms differences between signed execution payload by validators & beacon block. 
These are same data? 
or have some differences?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: Beacon block contains a field "execution payload", is that what you meant?

excerpts.author: johnydony
excerpts.content:
Yeah may be. 
Then beacon block is another term of `slot`??

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: No, a slot is a period of 12 seconds. It can contain a beacon block, but it can also be empty (e g. proposer failed to propose a block in time)

excerpts.author: johnydony
excerpts.content:
slot != beacon block. 
beacon block contains execution payload. 
execution payload != beacon block. 
Got it.

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: On Optimism, there is a 200k transactions / day limit after which they start throttling with higher gas prices. It was 100k / day previously. However, all of this doesn't matter because Optimism never processed more than 53k transactions a day as can be seen here: https://optimistic.etherscan.io/chart/tx

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: As to transaction costs, it's quite complicated as they use some form of their own gas, but as a general idea the cost of a L2 transaction is ~98% mainnet dependent. The Sequencer itself charges cents just like the sidechains.

is there something about calldata compression that makes it quite hard, or is it more likely it's just a lower priority for the teams?

excerpts.author: treyzania
excerpts.content:
> is there something about calldata compression that makes it quite hard
there's a few tricks you can do, but they're still special cases

excerpts.author: treyzania
excerpts.content: things like ether/erc20/erc721 transfers can be reduced a lot by doing lookups into the state with a proof when doing the fraud game, which adds complexity to the fraud proof verifier, but in the general case there isn't much you can do and have to put all the calldata there and execute it normally

excerpts.author: treyzania
excerpts.content: with zk rollups all of that proving happens off chain but it still has that extra complexity

excerpts.author: treyzania
excerpts.content: zksync *started* with only token transfers and doing those optimizations so it's already pretty small
